scenes.say: Week nine. Creativity, the last remaining commercial superpower, with creative director Brendan Willenberg.
scenes.title: Creativity: the last remaining commercial superpower
scenes.speaker: Brendan Willenberg

scenes.say: Commercial creativity is cheating. Same inputs as everyone else, but an unfair business advantage. And it's a method, not a gift.

lines.text: Creativity is a *method*, not a gift.

scenes.say: Step one is solving the real problem. Go from the brief, past the expected response, to the real problem, then the solution.

scenes.kicker: Extra gum · the Bad Breath Index
scenes.say: Extra's problem: shoppers don't notice gum at the checkout, because they're on their phones. So the Bad Breath Index put a gum prompt into the checkout itself.

scenes.title: Creativity thrives on *constraint*
scenes.say: Creativity thrives on constraint. Rexona couldn't buy media, so it earned it with Pitvertising. And V called out the whole energy drink category instead of copying Red Bull.

items.head: V Energy
items.sub: Can’t out-Red Bull Red Bull, so call out the category.

scenes.say: AI can speed-run the process. But on its own it gives similar, cheap ideas. Use it as your antagonist, not your assistant.
The takeaway? Be simple, not just smart. It's not creative if it's not commercial.

lines.text: It’s not creative if it’s not *commercial*.
